packages.name: Block Ball
packages.summary: A brick breaker with power-ups, combos and five level patterns.
packages.description:
Break every brick with the ball and your paddle. Some bricks drop power-ups: a wide paddle, a slower ball or an extra life. Break bricks back to back without touching the paddle for a combo. From level 3 some bricks need two hits. Your best score is saved.

Mouse or Left/Right moves the paddle, Space launches, P pauses.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Block Drop
packages.summary: Falling blocks with a ghost piece, hold, combos and levels.
packages.description:
Seven pieces from a shuffled bag, a ghost showing where the piece lands, a hold slot and the next three pieces. Clear rows back to back for a combo; every ten lines it gets faster. Your best score is kept.

Left/Right move, Up rotates, Space drops, C holds, P pauses.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: SciCalc
packages.summary: A scientific calculator that shows the answer as you type.
packages.description: Powers, roots, logs, trigonometry in degrees or radians, factorials and percent, with the usual order of operations. The answer appears while you type; the history keeps your last 30 sums.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Vulkan Cube
packages.summary: Spinning 3D shapes drawn through Quin OS's Vulkan.
packages.description: A cube, a pyramid, a diamond and a prism, drawn with the same Vulkan calls a program makes anywhere: instance, device, swapchain, shaders, render pass, pipeline, command buffers. Drag to turn the shape; 1-4 pick the shape, C changes the colours.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Hello Terminal
packages.summary: A colourful tour of what the Quin terminal can draw. Run: hello-terminal
packages.description:
Rainbow text, a boxed table, a colour strip, a progress bar and a spinner, all with plain printf and escape codes. After installing, type hello-terminal in Terminal.

Commands:
hello-terminal  —  print the tour (colours, a table, a progress bar, a spinner)
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: cowsay
packages.summary: A cow (or Tux, a cat, a robot) says whatever you like. Run: cowsay hi
packages.description:
cowsay hello prints a speech bubble with a cow. -t makes it think, -f tux|cat|robot picks someone else. Pairs well with the fortune package: fortune | cowsay

Commands:
cowsay MESSAGE  —  the cow says it
cowsay -t MESSAGE  —  the cow thinks it (thought bubble)
cowsay -f COW MESSAGE  —  pick who speaks: cow, tux, cat or robot
cowsay -h  —  short help
fortune | cowsay  —  speak a message read from another command (reads standard input)
Long lines wrap at 40 columns inside the bubble.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: fortune
packages.summary: A random saying about code and making things. Run: fortune
packages.description:
Thirty short lines, one picked at random each time. fortune -a prints them all.

Commands:
fortune  —  print one saying, picked at random
fortune -a  —  print all of them
fortune | cowsay  —  have the cow say it (needs the cowsay package)
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: weather
packages.summary: Today's weather and a 3-day forecast, right in Terminal. Run: weather Tokyo
packages.description:
Type weather for where you are, or weather and any city, place or airport code. You get the temperature and what it feels like, wind, rain, humidity and UV now, then the low, high and what to expect for the next days -- with weather emoji and colours that follow the temperature.

weather -f shows Fahrenheit, weather -d 1 only today. Data from wttr.in (no account needed).

Commands:
weather  —  the weather where you are (found from your connection)
weather CITY  —  any city, place or airport code, e.g. weather Tokyo or weather JFK
weather -f CITY  —  temperatures in Fahrenheit
weather -d N CITY  —  show N days of forecast (1 to 3)
weather -h  —  short help
Data comes from wttr.in over HTTPS, so it needs a network connection.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: todo
packages.summary: A to-do list that lives in Terminal. Run: todo add water the plants
packages.description:
todo add puts something on the list, todo done 2 ticks it off, todo star 1 keeps it on top, todo edit, todo rm and todo clear tidy up. Plain todo shows the list: open things first, how long ago you added them, and what's done.

The list is kept in ~/.todo, a plain text file.

Commands:
todo  —  show the list (open items first, starred on top, then done)
todo add WORDS  —  add something (todo a WORDS works too)
todo done N [N...]  —  tick off one or more numbers
todo undo N  —  not done after all
todo star N  —  star or unstar (starred items stay on top)
todo edit N WORDS  —  change the text of item N
todo rm N [N...]  —  delete one or more items
todo clear  —  delete everything that is done
todo help  —  short help
The list lives in ~/.todo (plain text, one line per item).
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: pomo
packages.summary: A focus timer with a big countdown, a chime and a notification. Run: pomo
packages.description:
pomo starts 25 minutes of focus (pomo 50 for any length, pomo 25 write report with a label). A big countdown fills the Terminal with a progress bar; space pauses, + and - change it by a minute. When time is up you get a desktop notification and a soft chime, then pick a 5 or 15 minute break.

Every finished focus session counts as a tomato for today: pomo stats shows them.

Commands:
pomo  —  25 minutes of focus
pomo MINUTES  —  any length, e.g. pomo 50
pomo MINUTES LABEL  —  focus with a label, e.g. pomo 25 write report
pomo break  —  a 5 minute break (pomo long: 15 minutes)
pomo stats  —  how many focus sessions you finished today
pomo help  —  short help
While it runs: space pause / resume, + / - add or remove a minute, r restart, q quit.
When time is up: b starts a break, f another focus, q quits.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.summary: Slide the tiles, join equal numbers, reach 2048. Run: 2048
packages.description:
The classic puzzle in Terminal, in colour. Arrow keys (or WASD / hjkl) slide every tile; two equal tiles that meet join into their sum, and each move brings a new 2 or 4. Reach 2048 -- or keep going.

u undoes a move, n starts again, q quits. Your best score is kept.

Commands:
2048  —  play
arrow keys, W A S D or H J K L slide all tiles
u  —  undo the last move
n  —  new game
q  —  quit
2048 -h  —  short help
Your best score is kept in ~/.2048.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: matrix
packages.summary: Digital rain like the film, in any colour. Run: matrix
packages.description:
Green code rains down the Terminal until you press a key. matrix -c picks the colour (blue, red, purple, gold, white or rainbow), matrix -s 1 to 5 the speed, and matrix -m "WAKE UP NEO" has the rain leave a message in the middle of the screen.

Commands:
matrix  —  green rain until you press a key
matrix -c COLOR  —  blue, red, purple, gold, white or rainbow
matrix -s N  —  speed from 1 (slow) to 5 (fast)
matrix -m "TEXT"  —  the rain leaves a message in the middle of the screen
Options combine: matrix -c rainbow -s 4 -m "HELLO".
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: hexview
packages.summary: Browse any file as hex, with a text column and number inspector. Run: hexview FILE
packages.description:
Open any file and see its bytes: offsets down the side, hex in the middle, the text on the right, colour-coded so zeros, text, spaces, control and high bytes stand apart. Move with the arrows, jump with g (255, 0xff, +16), find text with / or hex bytes with x (89 50 4e 47), and n / N step through the matches. The bar at the bottom shows the byte under the cursor as a number (8, 16, 32 and 64 bit, little or big endian) and in binary.

It reads a screenful at a time, so even a huge file opens at once. hexview -d FILE prints instead of browsing (add -s offset and -n length), and some-command | hexview - reads a pipe. Remove it any time from the Package Manager or with: pkg remove hexview

Commands:
hexview FILE  —  browse FILE: offsets, hex bytes, text and a number inspector
hexview -d FILE  —  print instead of browsing (colour on a terminal, plain in a pipe)
hexview -d -s OFFSET -n LEN FILE  —  print LEN bytes starting at OFFSET (decimal or 0x hex)
hexview -w 8|16|32 FILE  —  bytes per row when printing
some-command | hexview -  —  read standard input (prints, does not browse)
hexview --help  —  short help
While browsing:
  arrows or h j k l  —  move the cursor one byte / one row
  PgUp PgDn or b space  —  move one page
  Home End or G  —  jump to the start / end of the file
  g  —  go to an offset: 255, 0xff, +16 or -0x10
  /  —  find text (n next match, N previous, wraps around)
  x  —  find hex bytes, e.g. 89 50 4e 47
  e  —  little / big endian numbers in the bottom bar
  w  —  bytes per row: auto, 8, 16, 32
  a  —  show or hide the text column
  ?  —  help          q or Esc    quit
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: musicviz
packages.summary: A live spectrum of the music playing, right in the Terminal. Run: musicviz
packages.description:
Start a song in the Music Player, open Terminal and run musicviz: a colourful spectrum (bass on the left, treble on the right) dances to the real audio. Bars rise quickly and fall slowly, with a little peak cap on each one, and only the cells that change are redrawn so it stays smooth. The top line shows the song, the artist and how far along it is.

It also controls the player: space pauses and plays, n and p (or the arrow keys) change track. m switches the look (bars, mirror, dots) and c the colours (rainbow, fire, ocean, mono). Start in a look with musicviz -s mirror -c fire. Remove it any time from the Package Manager or with: pkg remove musicviz

Commands:
musicviz  —  show the spectrum of the song playing in the Music Player
musicviz -s STYLE  —  start in a look: bars, mirror or dots
musicviz -c COLOR  —  start in a colour: rainbow, fire, ocean or mono
musicviz --help  —  short help
While it runs:
  space  —  play / pause the Music Player
  n or Right arrow  —  next track
  p or Left arrow  —  previous track
  m  —  change the look (bars, mirror, dots)
  c  —  change the colours
  + and -  —  more or less sensitivity
  q or Esc  —  quit
It needs the Music Player to have a song (start one there first).
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Quincraft GPU (Mesa)
packages.summary: Draw Quincraft with Mesa OpenGL (on the host GPU with make launch GL3D=1). Choose it in Settings > Graphics.
packages.description:
Adds the Mesa OpenGL renderer to Quincraft (needs Quincraft 1.6.0 or newer). After installing, open Settings > Graphics and set Quincraft renderer to GPU (Mesa); Quincraft then starts with it. The Debug panel (the ` key) shows which renderer is drawing.

This is Mesa 24.0.9. Start Quin OS with 3D on the host (make launch GL3D=1) and Mesa's virgl driver draws on the host's graphics card; without that it uses its software driver, which is slower than the normal CPU renderer. Remove it any time from the Package Manager or with: pkg remove quincraft-gpu
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Quincraft
packages.summary: A complete voxel sandbox: endless worlds, caves, survival, crafting, mobs and day and night.
packages.description:
Build and survive in a world that never ends. Quincraft makes its own terrain from a seed: oceans and beaches, forests, deserts, snowy hills and mountains, with caves, lakes, lava and ores underground. Chop trees, dig, craft tools and armour, smelt ore in a furnace, farm wheat, and keep an eye on your health and hunger. When the sun goes down zombies, skeletons, creepers and spiders come out; by day pigs, cows, sheep and chickens wander the fields. Water and lava flow, sand falls, TNT explodes, and the weather changes. Choose Creative to fly and build with every block.

Worlds are saved in your home folder (quincraft) as you play. Everything -- textures, sounds, terrain -- is made by the game itself, so it needs no extra downloads. Remove it any time from the Package Manager.

Commands:
Controls
  W A S D  —  walk (double-tap W or hold Ctrl to sprint)
  Space  —  jump, swim up, fly up (Creative: double-tap Space to fly)
  Shift or X  —  sneak (won't fall off edges), fly down
  Mouse  —  look around
  Left button  —  hold to dig, click to hit mobs
  Right button  —  place a block, use doors/chests/furnaces/crafting tables, hold to eat food or draw a bow
  1 to 9 or mouse wheel  —  choose a hotbar slot
  E  —  inventory and 2x2 crafting (Creative: all blocks and items)
  Q  —  drop one item (Ctrl+Q the whole stack)
  `  —  show or hide the debug panel
  Esc  —  pause menu (options, save, quit to title)
Tips
  Punch trees for logs, make planks, a crafting table, then a wooden pickaxe. Furnace: 8 cobblestone in a ring.
  Torches (coal over a stick) light up caves and keep monsters away. Buckets pick up and place water or lava.
Options: render distance, field of view, mouse speed, volume, render quality, dynamic resolution and more.
packages.changes: 1.6.0: Settings > Graphics has a Quincraft renderer choice: CPU (the built-in renderer) or GPU (Mesa OpenGL, from the Quincraft GPU package); the Debug panel shows which one is drawing. 1.5.2: one right click places one block on an older Quin OS too (the 1.5.1 safety net let go a moment too late and placed a second block). 1.5.1: fixed placing a block once and then placing blocks again and again (the right mouse button release was never reported to the game; the updated Quin OS reports it, and on an older one a held right button now lets go by itself after a moment); mouse look is smoothed so the view no longer judders when the game runs faster than the window system. 1.5.0: much faster at large window sizes: the picture is now drawn on every CPU core at once (CPU Threads in Options chooses how many), triangles hidden behind others are skipped early, four pixels are shaded at a time, the sky and the final copy to the window are split over the cores, Anti-Aliasing no longer scans the whole picture, Auto Quality reacts within half a second and aims for 60 frames a second, and world loading takes less of each frame so walking does not stutter. Starting Quincraft no longer lowers your Render Distance to 6. 1.4.0: Window Size option in Options (up to 2560x1440; the picture is drawn at Resolution % of the window, so a bigger window is a sharper picture). 1.3.2: options to flip look left/right and up/down. 1.3.1: Options text fits the window. 1.3.0: now a Quin Studio project (open and build it in Studio). 1.2.0: mouse turns the right way, face shading on blocks, a Resolution slider (25-100%) and sharper default. 1.1.0: redrawn tools, anti-aliasing option, mipmapped textures (no shimmer), faster and fixed mouse look (needs the updated Quin OS), text that fits menus, dungeons, beds and animal breeding.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: QuinShift
packages.summary: Drag a file, press Shift, drop it on a slice: convert it or work on it without opening an app.
packages.description:
Hold the middle mouse button (the scroll wheel) on a file in the File Manager or on the desktop. A glass ring opens under the pointer. Move to a slice and let go. Scroll the wheel to switch the ring between Convert and Tools. Dragging a file and pressing Shift opens the same ring.

Convert: PDF to DOCX, TXT, JPG or PNG; pictures to PNG, JPG, PDF, DOCX, TIFF, BMP or ICO; text and Word files to PDF, TXT or DOCX. The result is saved next to the original and a bubble offers Open and Undo. Your original is never changed.

Tools for pictures: Compress (with the new size shown), Resize, Crop (aspect ratios, drag the box or type the size), Edit (brightness, contrast, saturation, rotate, flip, grayscale, auto levels), Add background (colour or gradient, padding, rounded corners, shadow, ratio), Annotate (boxes, lines, arrows, text) and Redact (black box, pixelate or blur). Every file also has Metadata, which shows what a file says about itself and saves a copy without camera and location data. PDFs have Images, which saves the pictures inside them.

QuinShift keeps running in the background after you start it; start it again to open its window, where you choose the key (Shift or Ctrl), switch the ring off, or set the JPEG quality. The full source is installed next to the app (the source folder in its install folder): open it in Quin Studio with Open Folder, change it and build it there.
packages.changes: 1.1.0: hold the middle mouse button on a file (in the File Manager or on the desktop) to open the ring; scroll the wheel to switch Convert and Tools. 1.0.0: first release.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Voice Recorder
packages.summary: Record your voice, keep it as a WAV file and listen to it again.
packages.description:
Press Record and speak: a live waveform and level meter show what the microphone hears, and the recording is written to Music/Recordings as it goes (mono, 48 kHz, 16 bit WAV), so it opens in any player, including the Music Player. Pause and carry on, turn the input gain up or down, then choose any recording from the list to play it, jump around by clicking its picture, rename it, delete it or open it in another app.

Needs a sound card with a microphone input (the AC97 card in the default setup). In a virtual machine the host's microphone has to be switched on for it, otherwise recordings are silent and the app says so.

The full source is installed next to the app (the source folder in its install folder): open it in Quin Studio with Open Folder, change it and build it there.
packages.changes: 1.1.1: levelling rewrites the file in place (no rename over the original). 1.1.0: cleaner recordings: Enhance (on by default) removes the microphone input's DC step and rumble with an 80 Hz high-pass, fades in, and levels the finished file so the loudest peak sits just under full scale; a too loud warning; saving no longer freezes the window. Playback always runs at the right speed.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: HD Audio Driver
packages.summary: Sound for computers with Intel High Definition Audio -- nearly every PC since 2005.
packages.description:
Quin OS has a built-in driver for the older AC97 sound chip. This driver adds the HD Audio controller that almost every desktop and laptop has instead (Intel, AMD and NVIDIA chipsets, and QEMU's intel-hda). Once installed, the Music player, videos, games and system sounds all play through it, and it starts with Quin OS every time.

It finds the codec's speaker, line-out and headphone outputs and plays through all of them, 16-bit stereo at 8 to 192 kHz, with volume control. Not supported yet: recording, HDMI and DisplayPort audio, and switching outputs when headphones are plugged in.

Terminal: lsmod shows it running, rmmod hda_audio stops it.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Lua for Quin Studio
packages.summary: Lua colours, an outline, Ctrl+R to run, and a Hello Lua project for Quin Studio.
packages.description:
Teaches Quin Studio the Lua language. Files ending in .lua get syntax colours, the Outline lists your functions, Ctrl+R runs the open file with the lua interpreter that comes with Quin OS, and a "Hello Lua" project appears under New from a Template.

Open Quin Studio's Extensions page to see it, or remove it here at any time.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Python for Quin Studio
packages.summary: Python colours and an Outline for Quin Studio (no interpreter on Quin OS yet).
packages.description: Syntax colours for .py files and an Outline of your def and class lines. Quin OS does not have a Python interpreter yet, so there is no Run command -- this is for reading and writing Python.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Web Languages for Quin Studio
packages.summary: JavaScript, JSON and CSS colours for Quin Studio.
packages.description: Syntax colours for .js, .json and .css files, with JSON and CSS property names picked out, and an Outline of your JavaScript functions and classes.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Shell and Config Files for Quin Studio
packages.summary: Shell scripts (Ctrl+R runs them), Makefiles, YAML, TOML and SQL in Quin Studio.
packages.description: Colours for shell scripts, Makefiles, YAML, TOML and SQL. Shell scripts run with sh when you press Ctrl+R, and a "Shell Script" project appears under New from a Template.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Archive Manager
packages.summary: Look inside .zip, .tar and .tar.gz files, unpack all of it or only what you pick, and pack folders and files.
packages.description:
Open an archive and see its files with their sizes, packed sizes and dates. Tick the ones you want and press Extract Selected, or Extract All: an archive that holds one folder unpacks beside itself, anything else gets a folder of its own, so nothing lands loose in your Downloads. A progress bar shows the file being unpacked, and Cancel stops it.

Pack Folder and Pack File make a .zip or a .tar.gz next to the original (it never overwrites an existing archive: the new one gets a number). Opens .zip, .jar, .docx, .xlsx and .pptx, .tar, .tar.gz, .tgz and .gz, and checks every unzipped file against its checksum.

Safe by design: names that start with / or climb out with .. are skipped and counted, so a bad archive can't write outside the folder you chose. Not supported yet: .7z, .rar, .xz, .bz2, password-protected zips and zip files over 4 GB.

Once installed, double-clicking an archive in the File Manager opens it here.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Notes
packages.summary: Quick notes that save themselves, with search and pinning.
packages.description:
Press + (or Ctrl+N) and start typing. The first line becomes the note's title; the list on the left shows every note, newest first, with the notes you pinned on top. The search box finds words in titles and text. Notes save a moment after you stop typing and when you close the window.

Every note is a plain text file in your Notes folder, so any other app can open it, and your notes stay yours if you remove Notes.

Ctrl+N new note, Ctrl+F search, Ctrl+S save now. Select text with Shift and the arrow keys or the mouse; Ctrl+C, X and V copy, cut and paste.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Calendar
packages.summary: A month at a glance, the day's agenda, repeating events and reminders.
packages.description:
See the month on the left and the selected day on the right. Double-click a day (or press N) to add an event with a title, time, location and notes; it can repeat daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, and a reminder can pop up 5 minutes, an hour or a day before. The arrow keys move between days, Page Up and Page Down between months, T jumps to today.

Events are saved in one standard iCalendar file (Calendar/calendar.ics in your home folder), so they move to and from other calendars: Import .ics adds the events of any .ics file, and opening an .ics file from the File Manager imports it here.

Reminders appear while Calendar is open, so minimise it rather than closing it. Times follow this computer's clock; time zones are not handled yet.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Passwords
packages.summary: Keep your logins in a vault that only your master password opens.
packages.description:
Store a login's title, user name, password, website and notes. The whole vault is one encrypted file: the key is made from your master password (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 150,000 rounds, a random salt) and the logins are sealed with AES-256-GCM, so a wrong password or a changed byte is caught before anything is shown. Nothing is stored in plain text, and the master password itself is never saved: if you forget it, nobody can open the vault, including us.

Copy buttons put a user name or password on the clipboard (a password leaves it again after 30 seconds). The generator makes passwords of 8 to 64 characters from the kinds of characters you choose, drawn from the system's random numbers, and a bar shows how strong a password is. The vault locks itself after five idle minutes and wipes the unlocked text from memory.

The vault is ~/.config/passwords/vault.qpv: back it up like any file.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: RSS Reader
packages.summary: Follow news sites and blogs from one window, without visiting them.
packages.description:
Add a feed's address (or pick BBC News, Hacker News, NPR or NASA) and the articles appear: your feeds on the left, the articles of the chosen feed in the middle, the article itself on the right. Understands RSS and Atom. Feeds load in the background while you read, and the last copy of each is kept on disk, so what you saw is still there without a network. Articles you have read are remembered; the number beside a feed counts the unread ones.

J and K (or the arrow keys) move between articles, R refreshes, A adds a feed, M marks an article read or unread, O opens it in the Browser. You can select and copy the text of an article.

Feeds that send only a headline show a note: open the article to read it. Your feed list is the text file ~/.config/rss/feeds.txt.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Maps
packages.summary: A street map of the world: drag, zoom, search for places and pin the ones you want to keep.
packages.description:
The map is OpenStreetMap. Drag to move it, use the wheel or the + and - buttons to zoom (double-click zooms in on a spot), and type a place into the search box: the matches are listed, and choosing one centres the map on it and marks it. Pin keeps a place in the list on the left so you can come back to it in one click. A scale and the coordinates of the middle of the map are always shown.

Map pictures load in the background and are kept on disk, so places you have looked at open again without the network and the servers are asked as little as possible. Arrow keys move the map, + and - zoom, / or F jumps to the search box.

Map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database Licence. Searching uses OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service and needs an internet connection.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Media Demos
packages.summary: Six small programs that show Quin OS's video, audio and font decoders at work.
packages.description:
Test programs for the media libraries inside Quin OS, for people who build or check them. H.264 Demo (edge264), VP9 Demo (libvpx) and AV1 Demo (dav1d) each play a short built-in clip in a window; MP3 Demo (minimp3) and Opus Demo (libopus) play a short built-in recording through the sound card; FreeType Demo draws text with real TrueType hinting.

They used to sit in the base system and the app launcher; they are here so the launcher only shows what you use. The video player, Music Player and Videos apps do not need this package.
packages.changes: First release: moved out of the base system.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: Graphics Demos
packages.summary: A spinning cube drawn three ways: Quin OS's OpenGL, its Vulkan, and the real Mesa.
packages.description:
Three small programs that draw the same rotating cube through Quin OS's OpenGL subset, its Vulkan subset, and the real Mesa 24 library (software renderer). For people who work on or check the graphics stack.

Mesa Cube Demo is large (13 MB) because it carries the whole Mesa library. They used to sit in the base system and the app launcher; they are here so the launcher only shows what you use.
packages.changes: First release: moved out of the base system.
packages.author: Quin OS Team

packages.name: PDF Viewer
packages.summary: Read PDF files and comic archives: zoom, search, follow links, copy text.
packages.description:
Open a PDF (or double-click one in the File Manager) and read it. The page you see is drawn by MuPDF, so fonts, images and colours come out the way the author made them. Left / Right or Page Up / Down turn pages, the mouse wheel scrolls and carries on to the next page, + and - zoom, W fits the width and P the whole page. Contents shows the document's outline; search finds a word on every page (Return jumps to the next hit, Shift+Return to the one before) and marks it in yellow. Drag across the text to select it and press Ctrl+C. Links inside the document jump to their page; web links open in the Browser. Dark inverts the page for reading at night. Password-protected PDFs ask for the password.

Also opens .cbz comic archives. Not supported yet: EPUB, XPS and SVG, filling in forms, annotations, printing.

The PDF Viewer uses MuPDF (c) Artifex Software, which is licensed under the AGPL-3.0, so this app and its source are AGPL-3.0 too. The full source is installed next to the app (see LICENSE.md in it).
packages.author: Quin OS Team
